    MA3700 · AIRCRAFT STRUCTURES 1

    Practical Aircraft Stress Analysis

    #Structural Idealization

    Pure thin-walled (monocoque) structures are resistant against tensile and internal
    pressure loads but offer little resistance to compressive and shear load. Stiffened
    thin-walled (semi-monocoque) structures have longitudinal stiffeners that carry
    most of the axial and bending stresses while the skin carries the shear stresses.

    The presence of stiffeners complicates the computation of bending and shear
    stresses around the walls of the section. Thus, stiffened thin-walled structures
    are idealized into skins and booms.

    Assumptions of structural idealization:

    • Booms are concentrated areas that carry only normal stress
      • Variation of normal stress in the boom due to bending is small
      • Normal stress is constant throughout cross-sectional area of the boom
      • Distance of the boom’s centroid to the mid-line of the wall thickness is small
    • Skins are thin and carry only shear stress
      • Shear stress is constant in the skin between booms
      • Shear stress is constant throughout the thickness of the skin

    Note that the cross-sectional area of a boom is small compared to the overall dimensions
    of the structure. For torsion of an open section structure, shear stress varies throughout
    the thickness of the skin.

    #Normal Stress

    Consider an actual skin with normal stresses. The actual skin can be idealized as an
    ideal skin, that carries shear, with the addition of booms, that carry normal stresses.

    The arbitrary stress distribution can be split into
    a uniform distribution and a linear distribution.

    Taking moments about CD,

    σn​⋅bt⋅21​b+21​(σm​−σn​)⋅bt⋅32​b=σm​Am​b

    21​b2tσn​+31​b2tσm​−31​b2tσn​=σm​Am​b

    61​b2tσn​+31​b2tσm​=σm​Am​b

    61​btσm​σn​​+31​bt=Am​

    where Am​ is the cross-sectional area of the boom

    💡
    Am​=6bt​(2+σm​σn​​)
    💡
    An​=6bt​(2+σn​σm​​)

    For an actual skin subjected to only axial stresses, σn​=σm​ such that the ratio of stresses σm​σn​​=1.

    Am​=6bt​(2+1)

    Am​=2bt​

    For an actual skin subjected to bending stresses, such that there is both tensile and compressive stresses, the ratio becomes σm​σn​​=−1.

    Am​=6bt​(2−1)

    Am​=6bt​

    For an actual skin subjected to bending stresses, such that there is only tensile or compressive
    stress, the ratio becomes σm​σn​​=0.

    Am​=6bt​(2+0)

    Am​=3bt​

    #Shear Stress

    Consider the equilibrium of the n-th boom in elemental length of the beam.

    (σz​+∂z∂σz​​dz)Br​−σz​Br​+q2​ dz−q1​ dz=0

    Br​∂z∂σz​​dz+q2​ dz−q1​ dz=0

    💡
    q2​−q1​=−∂z∂σz​​Br​

    where Br​ is the cross-sectional area of the boom

    Recall from analysis of thin-walled structures that,

    ∂z∂σz​​=∂z∂Mx​​(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Iyy​y−Ixy​x​)+∂z∂My​​(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Ixx​x−Ixy​y​)

    ∂z∂σz​​=Sy​(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Iyy​y−Ixy​x​)+Sx​(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Ixx​x−Ixy​y​)

    Substituting into the shear flow equation,

    q2​−q1​=−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sy​Iyy​−Sx​Ixy​​)Br​yr​−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sx​Ixx​−Sy​Ixy​​)Br​xr​

    q2​−q1​=−(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​)Br​yr​−(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​)Br​xr​

    Analyze the shear flow in an idealized section.

    Shear flow q0​ starts at some unknown position whereby s=0. Shear flow in the wall 1-2 is,

    q1​−q0​=−(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​)B1​y1​                 −(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​)B1​x1​

    Subsequent shear flow in the wall 2-3 is,

    q2​−q1​=−(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​)B2​y2​                 −(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​)B2​x2​

    Thus, shear flow q2​ in the wall 2-3 can be written as,

    q2​−q0​=−(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​)B1​y1​−(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​)B1​x1​                 −(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​)B2​y2​−(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​)B2​x2​

    From observation, shear flow for an n-th boom section is then,

    qs​−q0​=−(Sy​Iˉyy​−Sx​Iˉxy​) r=1∑n​Br​yr​−(Sx​Iˉxx​−Sy​Iˉxy​) r=1∑n​Br​xr​

    💡
    qs​−q0​=−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sy​Iyy​−Sx​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​yr​−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sx​Ixx​−Sy​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​xr​

    The computation of shear flow, due to shear forces, of open and closed section follows
    the same process used in the analysis of thin-walled structures. For an idealized section subjected to pure torque, the shear distribution is unaffected by the presence of booms.

    Sectional properties of booms are,

    💡
    Ixx​=∑Br​yr​2
    💡
    Iyy​=∑Br​xr​2
    💡
    Ixy​=∑Br​xr​yr​

    #Example

    Since the idealized section has an axis of symmetry, Ixy​=0.
    Only a vertical shear load of 10kN is applied, thus Sx​=0.

    Moment of inertia about x-axis is,

    Ixx​=∑Br​yr​2

    Ixx​=2(B1​y1​2+B2​y2​2+B3​y3​2+B4​y4​2)

    Ixx​=2[200(30)2+250(100)2+400(100)2+100(50)2]

    Ixx​=13.86×106 mm4

    The shear flow equation becomes,

    qs​−q0​=−Ixx​Sy​​ r=1∑n​Br​yr​

    qs​−q0​=−7.22×10−4 ∑Br​yr​

    Note that the RHS of the equation is the basic shear flow qb​
    of the idealized section when analyzing as an open section.

    q23​=(−7.22×10−4)(0)(100)=0

    Note that since the shear flow has not passed through a boom, Br​=0.

    Shear flow in the wall 3-4 is,

    q34​=(−7.22×10−4)B3​y3​

    q34​=(−7.22×10−4)(400)(100)

    q34​=−28.9 N/mm

    Shear flow in the wall 4-5 is,

    q45​=q34​+(−7.22×10−4)B4​y4​

    q45​=−28.9+(−7.22×10−4)(120)(50)

    q45​=−32.5 N/mm

    Repeating the process for the remaining walls,

    q56​=−32.5+(−7.22×10−4)(100)(−50)=−28.9 N/mm

    q78​=(−7.22×10−4)(250)(−100)=18.1 N/mm

    Taking moments about A,

    Sx​y−Sy​x=∮rqb​ ds+2A0​q0​

    0=∮rqb​ ds+2A0​q0​

    Shear force does not act through the shear center. Thus, there is
    shear flow due to the shear force and shear flow due to torque.

    Enclosed area of the entire section is,

    A0​=21​(120)(100+200)+240(200)+21​(240)(200+60)

    A0​=97200 mm2

    Note that A0​ is the mean area of the section.

    Since shear stress, and thus shear flow, is constant in the skin of an idealized section, the torque produced by the slanted sections can be rewritten as,

    ∫12​ rqb​ ds=2A12​q12​

    Torque in a thin-walled section.

    The shaded area A12​ can be obtained from geometry.

    A12​=21​(240)(100)+21​(240)(100+30)−21​(240+240)(30)

    A12​=20400 mm2

    0=∮rqb​ ds+2A0​q0​

    0=[r81​q81​L81​+2A12​q12​+2A78​q78​         −r45​q45​L45​−2A34​q34​−2A56​q56​]+2A0​q0​

    #Tapered Wing Spar

    #Taper in One Direction

    Consider a wing spar, in the yz-plane, and comprising of two flanges and a web.
    The wing spar, or beam, is of an elemental length dz. At the section z, the beam
    is subjected to a positive bending moment Mx​ and a positive shear force Sy​.

    The axial loads P1​ and P2​ can be resolved into a y-component and a z-component.
    The z-components can be determined by multiplying stress with the boom area.

    Pz​=σz,1​B1​

    Fz​=σz,2​B2​

    The y-components can be determined
    using similar triangles (shaded area).

    Py​=Pz​dzdy1​​

    Fy​=Fz​dzdy2​​

    Equating the internal shear force Sy​ with the external shear forces,

    Sy​=Sy(web)​+Py​+Fy​

    Sy​=Sy(web)​+Pz​dzdy1​​+Fz​dzdy2​​

    💡
    Sy(web)​=Sy​−Pz​dzdy1​​−Fz​dzdy2​​

    For an idealized beam, shear flow is constant along the web (the skin between booms).
    Thus, shear flow distribution of the web (skin) can be determined by replacing     Sy​ with Sy(web)​ in the shear flow equation for an n-th boom section.

    Since the web has an axis of symmetry, and is an open section,

    qs​−q0​=−(Ixx​Iyy​+Ixy​2Sy​Iyy​−Sx​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​yr​−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sx​Ixx​−Sy​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​xr​

    qs​−0=−Ixx​Sy​​ r=1∑n​Br​yr​

    💡
    qs​=−Ixx​Sy(web)​​ r=1∑n​Br​yr​

    #Taper in Two Directions

    Consider a beam tapered in two directions along its length and comprising an
    arrangement of booms and skin. The beam is subjected to positive bending
    moments Mx​ and My​, and positive shear loads Sx​ and Sy​.

    Note that if the beam is an open section, the shear loads are applied through
    the beam’s shear center, such that no twisting of the beam occurs.

    Similarly, the axial load Pr​ in the r-th boom can be resolved into a x-component,
    a y-component, and a z-component. The components can be determined using
    similar triangles.

    Py,r​=Pz,r​dzdyr​​

    Px,r​=Py,r​dyr​dxr​​

    Px,r​=Pz,r​dzdxr​​

    The applied shear load Sx​ is the resultant of the shear flows in the skin and webs, and
    the Px,r​ components of the axial load in the boom. Similarly, Sy​ is the resultant of the shear flows in the skin and webs, and the Py,r​ components in the boom.

    Sx​=Sx(web)​+r=1∑n​Px,r​

    Sx​=Sx(web)​+r=1∑n​Pz,r​dzdxr​​

    💡
    Sx(web)​=Sx​−r=1∑n​Pz,r​dzdxr​​

    Sy​=Sy(web)​+r=1∑n​Py,r​

    Sy​=Sy(web)​+r=1∑n​Pz,r​dzdyr​​

    💡
    Sy(web)​=Sy​−r=1∑n​Pz,r​dzdyr​​

    Note that the derivatives are the slope of the tapered length.

    The general equation for shear flow distribution is then,

    💡
    qs​−q0​=−[Ixx​Iyy​+Ixy​2Sy(web)​Iyy​−Sx(web)​Ixy​​]r=1∑n​Br​yr​−[Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sx(web)​Ixx​−Sy(web)​Ixy​​]r=1∑n​Br​xr​

    Note that the shear forces are replaced with the shear forces in the web (skin).

    For a closed section beam, the unknown q0​ can be determined by equating the moments due to external forces, Sx​ and Sy​, to the moments due to internal forces, Px,r​ and Py,r​.

    Sx​y−Sy​x=∮rqs​ ds−r=1∑n​Px,r​yr​+r=1∑n​Py,r​xr​

    Sx​y−Sy​x=∮r(qb​+q0​) ds−r=1∑n​Px,r​yr​+r=1∑n​Py,r​xr​

    💡
    Sx​y−Sy​x=∮rqb​ ds+2A0​q0​−r=1∑n​Px,r​yr​+r=1∑n​Py,r​xr​

    Note that an anticlockwise moment is positive and vice versa, hence the negative sign.

    #Wing Section

    The chordwise pressure distribution on an aerodynamic surface may be represented
    by shear loads (lift and drag) acting through the aerodynamic center together with a
    pitching moment M0​.

    The shear loads Sx​ and Sy​ can be transferred to the shear center of the section, with
    the addition of a torque T about the shear center. Assume there is no axial stresses
    in the booms and thus, only shear stresses are present.

    #Torsion of Multicell Wing Section

    The wing section consists of N cells and carries a torque T, which generates individual
    but unknown torques in each cell. Thus, each cell develops a constant shear flow qN​.

    Consider R-th cell of a wing section.
    From torsion theory, angle of twist is,

    ϕ=dzdθ​=2AR​G1​∮R​tq​ ds

    Let δ=∫tds​.

    ϕ=2AR​G1​[qR​∫12​tds​+(qR​−qR−1​)∫23​tds​+qR​∫34​tds​+(qR​−qR+1​)∫41​tds​]

    ϕ=2AR​G1​[qR​δ12​+(qR​−qR−1​)δ23​+qR​δ34​+(qR​−qR+1​)δ41​]

    ϕ=2AR​G1​[−qR−1​δ23​+qR​(δ12​+δ23​+δ34​+δ41​)−qR+1​δ41​]

    The general equation for angle of twist is then,

    💡
    ϕ=2AR​G1​[−qR−1​δR−1,R​+qR​δR​−qR+1​δR+1,R​]

    The above equation is applicable only if the cells are connected consecutively.
    Note that     δR−1,R​ and δR+1,R​ refers to the partiton walls between the cells.

    If sections of the cells are made from different materials,

    ϕ=2AR​1​∮R​Gtq​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​∮R​Gt/Gref​q​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​∮R​t∗q​ ds

    The general equation for angle of twist then becomes,

    💡
    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​[−qR−1​δR−1,R​+qR​δR​−qR+1​δR+1,R​]

    where Gref​ is a convenient reference value of the shear modulus

    #Shear of Multicell Wing Section

    For a wing section subjected to shear loads which do not act through the shear center,
    the resulting shear flow is due to the combined effects of the shear loads and torsion.

    Consider R-th cell of a wing section.The
    angle of twist due to transverse shear is,

    ϕ=2AR​G1​∮R​tq​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​G1​∮R​tqb​+q0,R​​ ds

    The general equation for angle of twist is then,

    💡
    ϕ=2AR​G1​[−q0,R−1​δR−1,R​+q0,R​δR​−q0,R+1​δR+1,R​+∮R​tqb​​ ds]

    where δ=∫tds​

    If sections of the cells are made from different materials,

    ϕ=2AR​G1​∮R​tqb​+q0,R​​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​1​∮Gtqb​+q0,R​​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​∮Gt/Gref​qb​+q0,R​​ ds

    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​∮t∗qb​+q0,R​​ ds

    💡
    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​[−q0,R−1​δR−1,R​+q0,R​δR​−q0,R+1​δR+1,R​+∮R​t∗qb​​ ds]

    where δ=∫t∗ds​ and t∗=Gref​Gt​

    Taking moments, of the shear flow in R-th cell, about O, the moment equation for that cell is,

    MqR​​=∮R​rqb​ ds+∮R​rq0​ ds

    MqR​​=∮R​rqb​ ds+2AR​q0,R​

    The moment of the external shear loads is thus, equal
    to the sum of moment of each cell in the wing section.

    💡
    Sx​y−Sy​x=R=1∑N​(∮rqb​ ds)+R=1∑N​(2A0​q0,R​)

    For tapered wing sections, the above equation has additional terms.

    💡
    Sx​y−Sy​x=R=1∑N​(∮rqb​ ds)+R=1∑N​(2A0​q0,R​)−r=1∑n​Px,r​yr​+r=1∑n​Py,r​xr​

    where subscript R represents the cell, and subscript r represents the boom

    #Example

    Ixx​=∑Br​yr​2

    Ixx​=2(2580)(165)2+2(3880)(230)2+2(3230)(200)2

    Ixx​=809×106 mm4

    Shear flow in the section is given by,

    qs​−q0​=−(Ixx​Iyy​+Ixy​2Sy​Iyy​−Sx​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​yr​−(Ixx​Iyy​−Ixy​2Sx​Ixx​−Sy​Ixy​​) r=1∑n​Br​xr​

    qs​−q0​=−Ixx​Sy​​∑Br​yr​

    qs​−q0​=−809×10686.8×103​∑Br​yr​

    qs​−q0​=−1.07×10−4∑Br​yr​

    Note that the RHS of the equation is the basic shear flow qb​.

    Analyzing as an open section

    A cut is made on the top skin of each cell, at skins 1-2, 2-3, and 3-4.

    q12​=q23​=q34​=0

    Note that since shear flow has not passed through a boom, Br​=0.

    q48​=q83​ and q27​=q75​

    Note that shear flow does not pass through a boom at 8 and 7.
    Thus, there is no change in shear flow from 4 to 3 and 2 to 5.

    q87​=0

    Since there are no booms at 8 and 7, shear flow is zero.

    Analyzing the shear flow for cell 1,

    q483​=q34​+(−1.07×10−4)B8​y8​

    q483​=0+(−1.07×10−4)(3230)(−200)

    q483​=69 N/mm

    Positive value indicates shear flow is in the direction from 4 to 3.

    Analyzing the shear flow for cell 2,

    q384​=(−1.07×10−4)B3​y3​

    q384​=(−1.07×10−4)(3230)(200)

    q384​=−69 N/mm

    Negative value indicates shear flow is in the opposite direction of 3 to 4,
    which corresponds to the result obtained earlier when computing     q483​.

    Analyzing the shear flow for cell 3,

    q275​=(−1.07×10−4)B2​y2​

    q275​=(−1.07×10−4)(3880)(230)

    q275​=−95.5 N/mm

    q56​=q275​+(−1.07×10−4)B5​y5​

    q56​=−95.5+(−1.07×10−4)(3880)(−230)

    q56​=0

    q61​=q56​+(−1.07×10−4)B6​y6​

    q61​=0+(−1.07×10−4)(2580)(−165)

    q61​=45.5 N/mm

    Shear flow

    Since the shear modulus for 7-8 is different from the rest,
    the equation for the angle of twist in each cell is thus,

    ϕ=2AR​Gref​1​[−q0,R−1​δR−1,R​+q0,R​δR​−q0,R+1​δR+1,R​+∮R​t∗qb​​ ds]

    where δ=∫t∗ds​ and t∗=Gref​Gt​

    δ=Gt/Gref​s​

    where Gref​=27.6 GPa

    δ12​=δ56​=27.6(1.22)/27.61023​=840

    δ23​=27.6(1.63)/27.61274​=783

    δ34​=27.6(2.03)/27.62200​=1083

    δ483​=27.6(2.64)/27.6400​=152

    δ572​=27.6(2.64)/27.6460​=174

    δ61​=27.6(1.63)/27.6330​=202

    δ78​=82.8(1.22)/27.61270​=347

    δ48​=27.6(2.64)/27.6200+50​=95

    δ83​=27.6(2.64)/27.6200−50​=57

    δ57​=27.6(2.64)/27.6230+50​=106

    δ72​=27.6(2.64)/27.6230−50​=68

    Angle of Twist for Cell 1

    2Gref​ϕ=A1​1​[0+q0,1​(δ34​+δ483​)−q0,2​δ83​+q483​δ483​]

    2Gref​ϕ=265×1031​[q0,1​(1083+152)−q0,2​(57)+69(152)]

    2Gref​ϕ=265×1031​(1235q0,1​−57q0,2​+10488)

    Angle of Twist for Cell 2

    2Gref​ϕ=A2​1​[−q0,1​δ83​+q0,2​(δ23​+δ83​+δ78​+δ72​)−q0,3​δ72​                         +(q275​δ72​−q483​δ83​)]

    2Gref​ϕ=213×1031​[−q0,1​(57)+q0,2​(783+57+347+68)                                −q0,3​(68)+95.5(68)−69(57)]

    2Gref​ϕ=213×1031​(−57q0,1​+1255q0,2​−68q0,3​+2615)

    Angle of Twist for Cell 3

    2Gref​ϕ=A3​1​[−q0,2​δ72​+q0,3​(δ12​+δ572​+δ56​+δ61​)                         +(q61​δ61​−q275​δ572​)]

    2Gref​ϕ=413×1031​[−q0,2​(68)+q0,3​(840+174+840+202)                                +45.5(202)−95.5(174)]

    2Gref​ϕ=413×1031​(−68q0,2​+2056q0,3​−7426)

    Moments Equation

    Taking moments about 2,

    Sx​y−Sy​x=∑(∮rqb​ ds)+∑ 2A0​q0,R​

    0=∑ rqb​s+∑ 2A0​q0,R​

    0=−r483​q483​L483​+r61​q61​L61​+2A1​q0,1​+2A2​q0,2​+2A3​q0,3​

    0=−1270(69)(400)+1020(45.5)(330)        +2(265×103)q0,1​+2(213×103)q0,2​+2(413×103)q0,3​

    0=265q0,1​+213q0,2​+413q0,3​−9868.35

    Total Shear Flow

    Solving these equations simultaneously,

    2Gref​ϕ=265×1031​(1235q0,1​−57q0,2​+10488)

    2Gref​ϕ=213×1031​(−57q0,1​+1255q0,2​−68q0,3​+2615)

    2Gref​ϕ=413×1031​(−68q0,2​+2056q0,3​−7426)

    0=265q0,1​+213q0,2​+413q0,3​−9868.35

    Shear flow q0​ for each cell is then,

    q0,1​=5.5 N/mm

    q0,2​=10.2 N/mm

    q0,3​=16.5 N/mm

    Subsituting the q0​ for each cell into any of the angle of twist equations,

    2Gref​ϕ=413×1031​[−68(10.2)+2056(16.5)−7426]

    ϕ=1.13×10−6 rad/mm
